compiled_state.description:
## Context

`src/rebar/llm/review_workflows.py` (101 lines) is strangler-fig scaffolding for
a cutover that is now being cancelled rather than completed. Its own docstring
(`:1-9`) states the design: express `review_ticket` as a one-step agent workflow
and provide "a parallel-run-and-diff that proves the workflow path yields the
SAME findings as the legacy path … this adds the equivalent workflow path + the
diff that gates a future cutover."

The legacy path it diffs against is the single-pass review engine
`operations._review_ticket_impl`, which ADR 0075 retired. There is no cutover to
gate: the legacy side is being deleted, so a harness whose only job is to compare
the two paths has no remaining purpose. `diff_review_paths` (`:70`) is also one
of the engine's few surviving callers (`:86`), so removing this module shrinks
what the engine-deletion slice has to clear.

The module is fully self-contained. Measured on `origin/main` at
`e2ed08b343a2be462de4433a93edbb5cbc062a52`, across `src tests docs scripts`
(excluding `tests/fixtures/`, which contains the name only inside recorded
agent-transcript text):

- `review_ticket_workflow_doc` (`def :20`) — called only at `:54`, inside this module.
- `run_review_ticket_as_workflow` (`def :39`) — called only at `:89`, inside this module.
- `diff_review_paths` (`def :70`) — called only at `test_review_as_workflow.py:51`.
- The module itself is imported exactly once outside itself:
  `test_review_as_workflow.py:14`, `from rebar.llm import review_workflows as RW`.
- `git grep -n 'review_workflows' -- docs` returns nothing, so no documentation
  describes it.

So the whole module plus one test is the entire blast radius. No production code
outside the file changes.

## Approach

Delete `src/rebar/llm/review_workflows.py` outright, delete the single test that
exercises it, and drop the now-unused import. Record the removal in the release
notes.

This slice deliberately leaves the review engine in place — removing it is a
later slice. That keeps this change a pure, independently reviewable deletion of
one self-contained module.

## Scope

In scope: `src/rebar/llm/review_workflows.py` (deleted),
`tests/interfaces/store/test_review_as_workflow.py` (trimmed),
`docs/release-notes.md` (entry added).

Out of scope, verified rather than assumed:

- `src/rebar/llm/operations.py` — the engine stays live through this slice. AC4
  asserts it is still present. `default_reviewer_id` loses its `:52` caller here
  but keeps its `operations.py:167` one, so it does **not** become dead yet.
- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/` — the executor and the `RunnerAgentStep` bridge are
  live, general machinery with many other users. This slice removes a *client* of
  the bridge, not the bridge. AC3 asserts the bridge's own test survives.
- `tests/interfaces/store/test_review_as_workflow.py:57`
  `test_public_review_ticket_entry_point_unchanged` — it calls the engine
  directly (`:61`) and never touches `review_workflows`, so it belongs with the
  engine's deletion, not here. It is left untouched.

## Testing

No new tests. One test is deleted and two are kept. Locate them by name, not by
line range.

**Delete `test_review_workflow_equivalent_to_legacy`** (`def :45`). It exists
solely to assert the strangler-fig equivalence being retired: it calls
`RW.diff_review_paths` (`:51`) and asserts `diff["equivalent"] is True`,
`legacy_findings == workflow_findings`, and
`legacy_summary == workflow_summary == "the summary"` (`:52-54`). With
`diff_review_paths` gone there is nothing left for it to assert.

**Keep `test_runner_agent_step_bridge_runs_an_agent_workflow`** (`def :21`). It
does **not** use `RW`: it builds its own workflow doc inline (`:24-36`) with
`"prompt": "code-quality"` and calls `runs.run` directly (`:38`), asserting the
bridge produced `findings[0]["detail"] == "z"` and `summary == "ok"`. That is
coverage of the surviving `RunnerAgentStep` bridge and must not be lost.

**Also in that file:** delete the `from rebar.llm import review_workflows as RW`
import (`:14`) — it becomes unused and ruff will flag it. Leave the other imports
(`rebar`, `FakeRunner`, `runs`, `Path`, `pytest`), which the two surviving tests
still use. Rewrite the module docstring (`:1-5`), whose current text — "The
``RunnerAgentStep`` path must match the legacy findings and summary while the
public entry point continues to use the legacy path" — describes exactly the
equivalence being deleted.

**Release notes.** Add an entry to the unreleased section recording that
`rebar.llm.review_workflows` and its three functions are removed, and why (the
strangler-fig cutover they gated is cancelled, not completed). Do not edit the
existing historical entries.

## Acceptance criteria

Each criterion is a single command whose stated result is the pass condition.

- [ ] **AC1 — the module is gone.**
      `test -e src/rebar/llm/review_workflows.py` exits non-zero.
- [ ] **AC2 — nothing references it or its functions.**
      `git grep -n 'review_workflows\|diff_review_paths\|run_review_ticket_as_workflow\|review_ticket_workflow_doc' -- src tests docs scripts ':!tests/fixtures/' ':!docs/release-notes.md'`
      prints nothing and exits 1. (`tests/fixtures/` holds the name inside recorded
      transcript text, and the release-notes entry AC5 requires necessarily names
      it; both would otherwise make this criterion unsatisfiable.)
- [ ] **AC3 — the bridge test survives.**
      `git grep -c 'def test_runner_agent_step_bridge_runs_an_agent_workflow' -- tests/interfaces/store/test_review_as_workflow.py`
      prints `1`.
- [ ] **AC4 — the engine is still present.**
      `git grep -c 'def _review_ticket_impl' -- src/rebar/llm/operations.py` prints `1`.
- [ ] **AC5 — the removal is recorded.**
      `git grep -c 'review_workflows' -- docs/release-notes.md` prints at least `1`.
- [ ] **AC6 — the trimmed module passes.**
      `pytest tests/interfaces/store/test_review_as_workflow.py` exits 0 and
      collects 2 tests, down from 3.
- [ ] **AC7 — the suite is green.** `make verify` exits 0.

file_impact.reason: Deleted whole (101 lines). Its three functions are called only from inside the module and from one test; no docs describe it.
Delete test_review_workflow_equivalent_to_legacy (def :45) and the RW import at :14; rewrite the module docstring at :1-5. Keep the bridge test at :21 and the engine smoke test at :57.
Add an unreleased-section entry recording removal of rebar.llm.review_workflows and its three functions; AC5 greps this file.
